canonical_question: Does the 'grain refinement' mechanism observed by Qi et al. [14] apply to single-crystal FeNiCrMn, or is it specific to the polycrystalline samples they simulated?

question_variants.question: Does the 'grain refinement' mechanism observed by Qi et al. [14] apply to single-crystal FeNiCrMn, or is it specific to the polycrystalline samples they simulated?
question_variants.resolution_summary: The paper by Qi et al. [14] studied both single-crystal and polycrystalline samples and observed grain refinement and twinning. However, the current study on FeNiCrMn did not observe twinning or grain refinement, suggesting the mechanism may be specific to CoCrFeMnNi or the conditions (e.g., strain rate, temperature) in the current study suppressed it.

answers.answer: Qi et al. [14] observed FCC to HCP phase transformation, stacking fault, grain refinement, and twinning in both single-crystal and polycrystalline CoCrFeMnNi HEAs under tension and compression.
answers.measurement_outcome: FCC to HCP phase transformation, stacking fault, grain refinement, and twinning occurred
answers.mechanism: Deformation mechanisms observed in both forms
evidence_spans: Qi et al. [ [14] ] analyzed the plastic deformation of single-crystal and polycrystalline CoCrFeMnNi HEAs under tension and compression using MD simulations. The simulation results indicated that during the plastic deformation of the HEA material, phenomena such as FCC to HCP phase transformation, stacking fault, grain refinement, and twinning occurred.

answers.answer: In the FeNiCrMn study, no twinning or FCC-to-BCC phase transformation was observed, and grain refinement was not mentioned as an active mechanism, suggesting the grain refinement mechanism from Qi et al. [14] may not apply or was not activated under the specific conditions of this study.
answers.measurement_outcome: No BCC atoms observed; twinning not observed
answers.mechanism: Plastic deformation mediated by Shockley partials only in this study
answers.boundary_limitation: Specific to FeNiCrMn composition and simulation conditions
evidence_spans: The primary dislocations observed were Shockley partial dislocations and stair-rod immobile dislocations.
No BCC atoms were observed in any of the three orientations, indicating that no FCC-to-BCC phase transformation occurred during tensile deformation.
The yield strength of the alloy was relatively insensitive to strain rate within the simulated range.
